decisions.rationale: torchmetrics SSIM is image-only (4-D/5-D, no mask or weights, batch-global data range); a [B, 1, N, 1] reshape with a (k, 1) kernel reproduces its score but cannot express masked/weighted local moments, coverage-based window exclusion, per-row data range, valid-only windows or arbitrary leading dims. The custom path is one native conv1d over stacked moment channels.
decisions.action: Keep the conv1d implementation and lock parity with torchmetrics on [B, 1, N, 1] inputs (reflect padding: score; valid padding: cropped map) and with a direct per-window NumPy reference for masks and weights.

known_divergences: default padding='valid' scores only windows fully inside the sequence; torchmetrics 1.9 averages reflect-padded windows (padding='reflect' matches it)
default data_range is the per-row target range; torchmetrics uses max(range(preds), range(target)) over the whole batch
moments are formed after a per-row shift, so the map differs from torchmetrics' uncentred E[x^2] - E[x]^2 at round-off level

decisions.rationale: LowRankMultivariateNormal has the same covariance structure but needs the factor materialised per row, has no per-sample masks, no flat (improper) priors and no nuisance posterior; the custom path uses native batched matmul, cholesky_ex and cholesky_solve on m x m systems.
decisions.action: Keep the Woodbury implementation and lock equality with MultivariateNormal and LowRankMultivariateNormal for proper priors.

known_divergences: flat prior directions return the improper p(a)=1 marginal, i.e. the restricted likelihood (REML) with its constants (tested against error contrasts); torch.distributions has no improper priors
rows whose posterior precision is not numerically positive definite raise instead of returning a jittered value
